research.name: The Coffee
research.size: At least 9 operating Lisbon locations listed on the official site, plus 2 “coming soon” locations (Alvalade and Praça das Flores).
research.recent_news: Reported on 2026-09-29 to be expanding in Portugal with three more units in Lisbon. Additional recent signals from hiring/posting activity point to Lisbon-based roles tied to European growth, supply chain, store performance, and implementation.
research.supplier_signals: Clear active expansion signal, with Lisbon serving as an operational hub for Europe-wide growth. The brand is also operating via a franchise model in Portugal, and hiring signals include supply chain and implementation roles, which are relevant for wholesale/vendor outreach.

research.name: The Standard, Lisbon
research.size: Planned hotel size: 170 guestrooms plus 24 adjacent apartments. No evidence found in the provided context of multiple Lisbon locations; this appears to be a single property in Palácio Santa Clara, Lisbon.
research.recent_news: Hyatt’s Standard brand was slated to open in Lisbon in 2026 at Palácio Santa Clara; some newer listing material suggests the opening may have shifted to Q1 2027. The project is being positioned as a high-profile lifestyle/boutique hotel in Lisbon, which is a growth signal for guest volume and premium amenity demand. Guest experience cues: the concept is described as design-led and experience-driven, with “anything but standard” programming and spaces for food, music, art, culture, rooftop/social use, a guest lounge, bar, restaurant, café, pool deck, event areas, and 24-hour in-room dining. It is intended to balance the building’s heritage with a contemporary, playful hotel experience.
research.supplier_signals: I found no clear official published list of local or sustainable suppliers tied specifically to The Standard, Lisbon. There is a general sustainability/local-rooted theme in the project messaging, but the strongest available sources emphasize design, heritage, and guest experience rather than procurement details. At this stage, the evidence for local/sustainable supplier preference is suggestive but not confirmed.
